report:
Based on high-quality clinical evidence, the answer is **no: ivermectin does not lower the risk of death in COVID-19**.

### Understanding the Evidence

* **Rigorous Clinical Trials:** Large, randomized controlled trials—such as the landmark TOGETHER trial published in *The New England Journal of Medicine*—and comprehensive Cochrane systematic reviews found no significant reduction in mortality, risk of hospitalization, or disease progression among COVID-19 patients treated with ivermectin compared to a placebo (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869).
* **Laboratory vs. Human Doses:** Initial interest stemmed from laboratory cell-culture experiments showing antiviral activity. However, achieving those antiviral concentrations in human lungs would require drug doses roughly 100 times higher than approved safe limits.
* **Flawed Early Research:** Early claims of reduced mortality were largely based on small observational studies or trials with severe methodological flaws and high risk of bias. When researchers re-analyzed the scientific literature while excluding low-quality or unreliable data, any apparent survival benefit vanished (https://www.bmj.com/content/373/bmj.n747, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8385940/).

Major public health bodies and medical organizations—including the World Health Organization (WHO), the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH), and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)—recommend against using ivermectin for the prevention or treatment of COVID-19.
